Closes InfraBuilder.cs's own documented note that embankmentMaterials() (infra.js:52-83) was 'NOT ported... GLB/FBX kit loading and material binding is a scene-assembly concern under the pure-data convention, not this builder's'. That reasoning is right for loadKit()/textureKit() (infra.js:13-45,87-93 -- they traverse an INSTANTIATED glTF scene graph, meaningless before a prefab exists) but embankmentMaterials() itself (infra.js:52-83, 32 lines) only builds two STANDALONE Material objects from texture files -- the exact shape of gap StatueMaterials.cs/JusticeHouseMaterials.cs already closed for landmarks.js. This is that counterpart for infra.js's river embankment: emb_wall (quay-wall ashlar, 0xb9b5ab, roughness 1, metalness 0) and emb_stone (coping/balustrade granite, 0xcfcabf, same roughness/metalness), both with their real albedo + normal maps bound (Assets/Art/Textures/quaywall*.jpg / quaystone*.jpg, already-imported CC0 assets from tools/fetch_infra_textures.py -- nothing fetched or re-exported here). InfraMaterials.For(kitMaterialName) resolves the embankment kit's own placeholder-material slot name to the real Material, the join key a scene-assembly consumer needs (same role MetroBuilder.Placement.Kind documents for its own kit). InfraBuilder.cs itself is NOT edited -- one of the five files other agents are touching right now.

NOT PORTED, reported rather than guessed at: roughnessMap (infra.js:72,79 -- a dedicated linear PBR channel with no stock URP/Lit equivalent; Lit only takes one combined Metallic-Smoothness map, and a roughness-only greyscale texture is not that map and is also the INVERSE channel, so binding it there would silently misrender rather than approximate) and envMapIntensity (0.3/0.35 -- URP's stock Lit shader has no reflection-intensity float, only an Environment Reflections on/off toggle, the identical gap JusticeHouseMaterials.cs already reports for the same Three.js property on justice_house.fbx).

note: Closes ParkBuilder.cs's own documented note: 'NOT covered: courtTexture()'s painted line/arc canvas (parks.js:83-122, ~40 lines -- solid category colour only, ParkBuilder.CourtColor)'. Unlike the brand signs or the metro plates, courtTexture() needs NO font at all -- the JS only ever strokes axis-aligned rectangles, straight H/V segments and one circle (the outer court border on every kind; a centre line + centre circle on soccer/basketball/multi; two key boxes on basketball; a service-box frame + 2 tramlines + 1 service line on tennis) -- so this is a full, verifiable 1:1 port of the entire function, not a partial one: all 40 lines. Built as a real Texture2D pixel buffer (no DOM canvas), same technique as LandmarkSignage.cs/MetroSignage.cs. ParkBuilder.cs itself is NOT edited (it is pure data, no Material objects anywhere in that file by design) -- this sibling class is where a consumer resolves ParkBuilder.CourtColor's own `kind` string into the full line-marked Material via BuildMaterial(kind).
verified: tools/_probe_cityinfra.mjs, RUN directly: confirms the court canvas's own dimensions (256x160), line width (4) and stroke alpha (rgba(255,255,255,0.9)) are present verbatim in the live src/parks.js text, then INDEPENDENTLY re-derives the exact touched-pixel count per sport kind by literally re-running the same rect/line/circle rasterisation algorithm this task's ParkCourtTextures.cs uses (soccer=4182, basketball=5270, tennis=6096, multi=4182, unknown/default=3008 -- all printed). Because every stroke boundary in courtTexture() lands on an EXACT integer pixel grid at line-width 4 (half-width 2), the rect/line portions of this count are not an estimate -- they equal the closed-form frame-area formula 2*lineWidth*(w+h) per strokeRect/length*lineWidth per line -- only the one circle is a discrete ring sweep. Assets/Editor/Probes/CityInfraProbe.cs (PrintParks) builds the REAL ParkCourtTextures.Build(kind) texture and reads GetPixels32() back, counting pixels that differ from the base fill colour -- its PARK_COURT_*_TOUCHEDPX lines must equal the .mjs script's numbers above EXACTLY (same algorithm, same integer grid, zero tolerance expected) -- written but NOT run (no editor access); only the Node-side computation above was executed.
